chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) pronounced takbir over Sahl ibn Hunayf, who was a companion of Badr, with five takbirs. Then he walked for a moment, then placed him (in the grave), and pronounced five other takbirs over him. He did this until he had pronounced over him twenty-five takbirs.

key_terms.سَهْلِ بْنِ حُنَيْفٍ: Sahl ibn Hunayf (a companion of Badr)

ai.seo_question: How many takbirs did Imam Ali perform in the funeral prayer according to this narration?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the unique ritual of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) praying over Sahl ibn Hunayf, a companion of the Prophet, by performing twenty-five takbirs in five sets of five with brief pauses. This practice is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it provides a distinct precedent for the number of takbirs in the funeral prayer, differentiating it from the Sunni tradition of four takbirs, and underscores the reverence due to the Ahl al-Bayt's specific liturgical innovations.
